last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Mon 08-31, day 20, and he came back a SECOND time the same day (16:24, after the 08:34 Deep-Dive). Short Table Rehearsal, three fires, all three landed. THE HEADLINE — THE KEKKU AMBUSH FIRED CLEAN AND wrong-verb-direction IS CLOSED. On 08-30 kekku and sollu were one jammed wire: three ear-misses read kekkala as "said", and the closing fire came back sonnen where kekkuren was owed. The soak dose shipped 08-30; I held the verb out of every production slot this morning on purpose to keep the ambush clean. This afternoon a maami mask asked who was going to find out whether mama was coming to eat — normal table talk, no warning, no framing — and he gave "naan avan kitta kekkuren" instantly. Right verb, right direction, kitta sitting exactly where it belongs. Tested and closed. The dose+ambush recipe (commission it, hold the word out of chat, ambush it unannounced days later) is now proven on a second tag — write it down as method, not luck. PERSON-MARKER HELD UNDER THE EXACT TRAP THAT BROKE IT THIS MORNING — BUT I DID NOT CLOSE IT. Third fire was a deliberate echo trap: athai in the doorway says "naan kadaikku poren" and THEN asks him where mama is going, so the last tail in his ear was -en and the answer needed -aaru. This morning that inversion happened twice inside four minutes. This time he gave "avaru kovil-ku poaaru" — the tail on the PERSON, not on the echo. Deliberately left OPEN: one clean instance on the same day the soak dose rendered (and he almost certainly has not heard the dose yet) is not a close. Trap it again tomorrow at speed. THE -ttu-kren DEBT PAID, AND HE GENERALISED IT UNPROMPTED. Opened by paying off the pocket hook from this morning — the self-benefactive -kko- infix, gifted with paathukkren / eduthukkren / pottukkren and the reason it matters at that table: it is the polite exit that is not a refusal, you are not saying no to her, you are saying the job is already mine (the declining set, the campaign's through-line). Four lines later, asked to wave the maami off her ladle, he fired "podhum podhum, naane paanikkiren" — podhum doubled like a real speaker, and the -kko- carried onto pannu, a verb I never handed him. Logged HINTED, not cold, because I laid three worked examples down in the same breath — but the generalisation to a novel verb is the interesting part, and it is the opposite of this morning's echo behaviour. Note also: frame:myself-thukka is flagged EAR ONLY in the lexicon and he just produced it. NO NOUN EXIT ALL SESSION. After this morning's new noun-for-verb tag, I watched every production slot for the noun dodge and it never came — three asks, three verbs. One afternoon is not a trend; keep watching. NEW SLIP, honorific-pronoun: "naan avan kitta kekkuren" — avan is the cousin your age, the mama is elder and wants avaru. Recast in one clause (the respect lives on the PRONOUN, not only on the verb tail) and he used avaru correctly one line later, in the very next fire. Related to the closed stranger-nga but not the same surface: that one was -nga on verbs, this is rank carried by the noun itself. 1x — watch, do not commission. ALSO NOT TAGGED, WATCH IT: "poaaru" for poraaru — the present -r- dropped out of the stem when the honorific tail went on, and he wrote poren clean this morning. That is the standing law running live (make the stem automatic and the tail comes free) except in reverse: the heavy tail cost him a piece of the stem. One data point, no tag yet. THE FIELDING KNOCK FROM THIS MORNING went unanswered on the phone and I collected it in-session instead — decoded innum konjam saapdunga for him with no grading (break contract) and then re-fired it as the first mask beat, where it became his podhum/pannikkren fire. An unanswered knock is not a dead knock; it is a scene to reuse. SOAK ORDER LEFT STANDING — deliberately did not overwrite this morning's person-marker minimal pairs. That dose rendered today and has not done its work yet; a same-day overwrite would bury it. TONIGHT'S MISSION, one op with two doors: the morning's where-are-you-going answer still counts, and the guaranteed trigger is the plate — she pushes food three times a day, and now he can take the job off her instead of only refusing it (naane pannikkren / naane eduthukkaren). Debrief tomorrow, either door. TOMORROW OFFERED: Table Rehearsal at full speed, athai and maami, no thinking time, person tails under pressure; low-power twin is Ear Day on the kekku tape with nothing to answer. TRAILER LEFT HANGING: the present/future toggle on the verb we just fixed — kekkuren vs keppen. He fires the toggle; the ear is what is behind (it sits in the ticket's EAR block as comfortable-but-unheard). One letter, and that is the ambush.

soak_order.focus: THE PERSON TAIL, AND NOTHING ELSE MOVING. He used the nee-tail on himself and then the naan-tail on her inside four minutes: the ending is an echo of whatever he heard last, not a choice. Permute ONLY the person marker on two verbs he already owns, in matched frames, back to back: நான் போறேன் / நீ போற, நான் சொல்றேன் / நீ சொல்ற. Do NOT permute tense, do NOT permute the verb, do NOT bring in a third person — -en is me, -a is you, and the contrast is the whole payload. This is the minimal-pair recipe that converted போனோம் in one cycle. Every other lexical item from lexicon.json. Never name a rule.
